requirements.title: STOP initiates normal termination
requirements.source: 11.4 p1; the integer process-status recommendation in p2 is a separate profile qualification.
requirements.definition: Executing STOP initiates normal termination. The optional integer process-status mapping is processor-dependent and recommended rather than universally required.
requirements.oracle: Use an external driver to supply input, inspect stdout and a closed output file, and judge termination. The posix-stop-code facet explicitly chooses status 200 as a processor-profile expectation; it must not be mistaken for a compiler crash or silently promoted to a universal Fortran requirement.

requirements.title: STOP has independently optional stop-code and QUIET parts
requirements.source: 11.4 R1162, J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF228, printed214, line15.
requirements.definition: A STOP statement has an optional stop-code followed by an independently optional comma and QUIET=scalar-logical-expr. The code may be omitted while QUIET is present. QUIET is a scalar logical expression, not necessarily a literal or constant expression, and this production does not require default logical kind. Stop-code type/kind and source-form rules retain their own owners.

pending.no-code-form: PENDING a complete ordinary main program with bare STOP, compiled as a positive control without executing termination. Syntax admission is not a new normal-termination or host-status effect.
pending.code-and-quiet-optionality: PENDING finite compile controls crossing absent/default-integer/default-character code with absent, false and true QUIET, including STOP with no code and a comma-QUIET suffix. Use defined scalar expressions and preserve R1164/C1176 owners.
pending.quiet-scalar-logical: PENDING source-qualified scalar-logical admission and otherwise complete wrong-type or rank-one QUIET contrasts with scalar-logical repairs. C1007 and assumed R403/C401 supply the inherited predicates; adjudicate one canonical owner/cause rather than clone their violations.
pending.quiet-expression-admission: PENDING a defined ordinary logical variable or expression as QUIET and, only where supported, a valid nondefault logical kind. No constant-only or default-kind-only restriction may be invented; compile controls do not establish evaluated runtime suppression.
pending.separator-and-order-source-gate: PENDING complete contrasts for the required comma, QUIET keyword/equal sign, ordering and nonrepetition. Exclude another valid statement parse and repair only the intended syntactic relation; source-form or unrelated expression errors cannot substitute.

requirements.oracle: Source-valid compile/positive-controls and single-predicate diagnostic/repair pairs in ordinary program contexts, with complete source, exact intended causes and legitimate origins reviewed before any fixture.
requirements.oracle_limitation: 4.2 requires reporting capability, not fatal rejection, fixed wording or a printed code. Unsupported STOP/QUIET facilities, source echoes, other errors and internal/resource failures are not qualifying diagnostics. No new fixture, role designation or runtime evidence is supplied.

requirements.title: ERROR STOP has independently optional stop-code and QUIET parts
requirements.definition: An ERROR STOP statement has an optional stop-code and an independently optional following comma-QUIET scalar-logical expression. Its syntax does not require a code, a constant QUIET value or default logical kind. Admission of the statement is distinct from executing error termination and from the source-form rules for its two keywords.

pending.no-code-form: PENDING a complete ordinary main program containing bare ERROR STOP, compiled but not run as a syntax positive control. A successful compilation supplies no error-termination, image or nonzero-status observation.
pending.code-and-quiet-optionality: PENDING compile controls for absent/default-integer/default-character code with omitted or explicit true/false QUIET, including no code with QUIET. Keep all operands scalar and defined if the program were executed.
pending.quiet-scalar-logical: PENDING exact C1007 and R403/C401 source relations for QUIET type/rank, with a valid scalar-logical repair and one causal owner. Do not credit a generic ERROR STOP implementation failure or an invalid stop-code instead.
pending.quiet-expression-admission: PENDING defined logical-variable/expression controls and separately qualified supported logical-kind boundaries. Any evaluated-expression runtime test belongs to the corresponding output/termination effect, not this compile admission.
pending.separator-and-order-source-gate: PENDING single-predicate suffix-order, comma, keyword/equal-sign and repetition contrasts in complete contexts. Keep invalid syntax diagnostics separate from compiler/launcher process failure and error termination of a valid program.
pending.source-form-keyword-boundary: PENDING canonical free/fixed source-form relations: ERROR and STOP are adjacent keywords and are not a blank-optional pair in Table6.2. An omitted separating blank in free form belongs to the lexical owner, not a new error-termination effect; any fixed-form control retains actual column/line rules.

requirements.oracle: Complete syntax admissions and genuinely source-isolated diagnostic repairs, without executing the ERROR STOP programs or duplicating canonical expression/source-form cases.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No fatal-status, standardized-English, rule-code or unsupported-feature proxy. This source-only entry does not claim an error-termination trace, a process-status value or a multi-image result.

requirements.title: A stop-code is scalar default character or scalar integer
requirements.definition: A stop-code is a scalar default-character expression or a scalar integer expression; C1176 additionally restricts the integer alternative to default kind. These are expressions, not literal-only or constant-expression productions. Character length, integer sign and host process-status representability do not supply additional local restrictions.

pending.default-character-admission: PENDING complete compile controls for default-character literals and defined scalar character variables/expressions, including zero length. Do not interpret an empty string as omitted syntax or infer a particular printed message or exit status.
pending.integer-admission: PENDING complete default-integer compile controls with zero, positive and negative representable values. The syntax has no five-digit-literal or host-exit-range limit; avoid integer overflow and keep C1176 kind qualification separate.
pending.defined-expression-admission: PENDING defined ordinary scalar variables and simple integer/character expressions for both statement kinds. A future effect oracle must independently bind the evaluated value and termination; compile acceptance alone proves neither.
pending.other-type-source-gate: PENDING otherwise complete real/logical stop-code contrasts and one-expression integer/character repairs. Resolve the R1164 alternative and inherited C1008/C1009 causes before selecting a canonical case; unrelated typing or feature errors earn no credit.
pending.scalar-source-gate: PENDING rank-one default-integer or default-character expression contrasts with same-type scalar repairs. Assumed R403/C401 is the canonical scalar premise; vector size one does not make an expression scalar.
pending.default-character-kind-source-gate: PENDING C1008's default-character restriction with a supported, demonstrably distinct nondefault character kind and a default-kind repair. No arbitrary kind code, mandatory ISO10646 support or unsupported-kind diagnostic is a substitute; leave the contrast gated where no second kind is available.

requirements.oracle: Finite complete type/rank/expression admissions and source-isolated canonical negatives. Defined scalar values and actual supported kinds are prerequisites, independent of any compiler's diagnostic wording.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No new BOZ claim, undefined operand evaluation, character-storage model or universal process-status truncation oracle. Numbered reporting capability is not required rejection or a prescribed message.

requirements.title: An integer stop-code has default kind
requirements.source: 11.4 C1176 associated with R1164, physical PDF228, printed214, line19.
requirements.definition: The scalar integer expression used as a stop-code has default integer kind. The restriction applies to the integer alternative, not to QUIET or character length. Default kind is identified by the language's kind relation, not by a fixed kind number, storage width or process-status range.

pending.default-kind-admission: PENDING complete STOP and ERROR STOP compile controls using default integer declarations/literals or an explicit kind equal to KIND(0), with representable defined scalar values and otherwise valid syntax.
pending.supported-nondefault-kind-exclusion: PENDING a processor-qualified distinct supported integer kind, an otherwise valid scalar stop-code of that kind, and a default-kind repair. Establish support and distinctness before any diagnostic contract; another integer kind is not presumed to exist or to have a particular number.
pending.kind-identity-source-boundary: PENDING exact type/kind/source relations separating default integer kind from value range, literal spelling and the host's exit-status interface. Reuse a meaningful canonical kind/profile witness where justified rather than add a no-op or duplicate another owner's unsupported-kind test.

requirements.oracle: An actually supported nondefault-kind violation paired with a valid default-kind control, with precise source attribution and complete cause review. Admission is compile/positive-control evidence, not a status-value effect.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No kind=4/8 or word-size assumption, unsupported-kind credit, narrowing/overflow repair, mandatory fatal status or printed C1176 requirement. The unchanged status200 calibration is not a new C1176 case.

requirements.title: Executing ERROR STOP initiates error termination
requirements.source: 11.4 p1 second sentence, physical PDF228, printed214, lines20-21; canonical termination semantics are5.3.7.
requirements.definition: Execution of ERROR STOP initiates error termination, not normal termination, return from a procedure or a failed-image event. Under5.3.7, initiation on an image propagates to all images that have not already initiated error termination; program termination occurs when all images have terminated or failed. The recommendation to propagate as quickly as possible is not a numeric timing guarantee. A nonzero shell status alone does not establish these semantics.

pending.initiating-image: PENDING a complete valid program and independent external lifecycle driver with an observed pre-ERROR-STOP event, actual execution/termination trace and a guard against subsequent work. A lone unreachable marker, compiler acceptance, arbitrary nonzero exit or crash is insufficient. Source-qualify the observable distinction from normal termination before claiming this effect.
pending.program-wide-image-propagation: PENDING qualified canonical5.3.7 multi-image evidence using actual image-count/launcher configuration, independently identified participating images and safely ordered pretermination events. Observe the complete process/image lifecycle; do not infer all-image initiation from the initiating process's status or one missing output record.
pending.stopped-and-failed-image-source-boundary: PENDING exact5.3.6/5.3.7 relationships for active, normally stopped, already-error-terminating and failed images. A failed image is not an ERROR STOP event; no reference to unavailable/undefined failed-image data or requirement that a failed image execute a later guard is admissible.
pending.team-and-segment-source-gate: PENDING initial/current-team and segment-ordering premises before any multi-image fixture or reuse.5.3.7 concerns all program images, not merely a current subteam. STOP is an image control statement under11.7.1; ERROR STOP must not be treated as that normal-termination synchronization or as a fabricated SYNC ALL.

requirements.oracle: Real run/effect evidence through a source-reviewed termination/lifecycle mechanism or qualified canonical reuse. Entry, intended statement execution and whole-run completion must be externally established with independent events and correct image/configuration bindings.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The applicable termination owner in this pinned draft is5.3.7, not11.6, which describes NOTIFY WAIT. No mandatory error exit code, signal, crash, post-error file flush, C ABI or fixed propagation deadline is inferred. Missing lifecycle/launcher capability leaves the facet pending or an observation unqualified, not passed.
requirements.dependencies: 5.3.4-.7;11.5;11.7.1/.2;11.4 R1163/p2;4.2p1-p2/p5-p8;canonical termination, image/team and segment owners.

requirements.title: A terminating image's specified stop code is made available by a processor-dependent method
requirements.source: 11.4 p2 first sentence, physical PDF228, printed214, lines22-23.
requirements.definition: When an image is terminated by STOP or ERROR STOP, a specified stop code is made available in a processor-dependent manner. The method is not universally a process exit status, stdout, stderr, formatted text or an exact message. The integer/other-status recommendations and the formatted-output recommendation are separately classified; QUIET=true suppresses code output without defining an exit status or erasing every possible non-output availability mechanism.

pending.integer-code-interface: PENDING a specific reviewed processor interface/profile and complete program with an independently known representable default-integer code. Bind the actual selected code, normal/error termination and the documented availability channel. The preserved POSIX200 calibration is a candidate relation, not a new link or generalized integer-status promise.
pending.character-code-interface: PENDING a qualified processor method for a known default-character code, with actual run evidence and a precise source-reviewed decoder. Character stop-code syntax does not prescribe display wording, a stream, encoding, numeric status or nonempty length; absent-code cases impose no invented code value.
pending.statement-kind-and-termination-binding: PENDING finite STOP/ERROR STOP availability observations with complete per-image/statement/configuration attribution and lifecycle guards. Keep the code's availability distinct from proof of the different termination modes and from recommendation-only numeric status mappings.
pending.quiet-true-nonoutput-interface: PENDING an explicitly qualified non-output availability mechanism for a specified code under QUIET=true, if one can be observed. Do not demand forbidden code output, infer availability from silence, or translate a missing documentary/testing mechanism into a language failure or a success-shaped default.

requirements.oracle: An actual independently specified code joined to a reviewed processor-defined interface and successful complete execution evidence. Unknown or unavailable mechanisms are explicit source/documentary/profile gates, not generic output or exit-code fallbacks.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Documentary/profile prerequisites are qualification gates, not a new universal documentation mandate. No universal process concept, exact code mapping, 8-bit truncation, status200, nonzero error status or literal STOP/ERROR STOP text is added. All new facets remain pending; historical observations and S11.4-001 remain unchanged.
requirements.dependencies: 11.4 R1164/C1176/p2-p4/note2;5.3.4-.7;4.2p5-p8;actual processor interfaces;unchanged S11.4-001 and its explicitly selected posix-stop-code profile.

requirements.title: Without QUIET=true, signaling exceptions require an identifying warning on ERROR_UNIT
requirements.source: 11.4 p3 condition and first bullet, physical PDF228, printed214, lines29-32.
requirements.definition: If QUIET is omitted or its scalar logical expression is false and any exception is signaling on the terminating image, the processor issues a warning identifying which exceptions are signaling, on the unit identified by ISO_FORTRAN_ENV's ERROR_UNIT. This conditional runtime warning is required, unlike the following stop-code-output recommendation. The metadata's not-required compile-diagnostic obligation does not weaken that runtime requirement.

pending.quiet-omitted: PENDING a complete STOP/ERROR STOP run with omitted QUIET and a genuinely signaling supported flag. Qualify IEEE module/flag and any needed halting control, establish the flag in the termination-containing procedure, and observe an identifying warning plus independent entry/termination evidence.
pending.quiet-false: PENDING the corresponding explicit false logical expression with the same qualified signaling setup. Include a source-valid quiet-flag contrast without inventing a required warning when no exception is signaling. A merely compiled program or unrelated runtime warning is not the effect.
pending.multiple-signaling-flags: PENDING a supported distinct finite flag set and independent expected identities, using actual IEEE_SET_FLAG/GET_FLAG interfaces and no duplicate FLAG elements. Require identification of the intended signaling exceptions, not an exact English vocabulary, warning count or order. Do not force unsupported flags or provoke undefined arithmetic.
pending.error-unit-routing: PENDING a source-reviewed external observation method for the actual preconnected ERROR_UNIT and its processor routing, with separate known user-output controls. ERROR_UNIT may equal OUTPUT_UNIT and is not universally unit0 or OS stderr; the warning's required unit cannot be replaced by whichever captured stream happens to contain text.
pending.terminating-image-and-scope-state: PENDING exact per-image and procedure-entry flag-state premises.5.3.4 gives each image its own floating-point status;17.3p3 can quiet flags on entry to another procedure. Do not set a flag in a caller and terminate inside an unqualified helper, rely on unused arithmetic to signal, or infer another image's flags from one report.

requirements.oracle: Real run/effect records join supported flag setup, independently specified expected identities, the actual terminating statement/image, ERROR_UNIT routing and externally observed completion. Compiler/configuration-specific output decoding needs review and may not accept generic exception-looking text.
requirements.oracle_limitation: IEEE modules and some flags are processor dependent; IEEE_SUPPORT_FLAG and any IEEE_SUPPORT_HALTING prerequisites must be honored. Do not call IEEE_SET_HALTING_MODE when support is false or assume an initial halting mode. Signaling flags are not signaling-NaN values or proof of a trap. The p3 second bullet remains a recommendation, and no native observation/profile is authored here.

requirements.title: QUIET=true suppresses signaling-exception and stop-code output
requirements.definition: When QUIET is present and its scalar logical expression is true, no output of signaling exceptions or the stop code is produced. This is a required suppression for STOP and ERROR STOP, not merely a recommendation. It does not suppress arbitrary earlier user output, remove termination, prescribe a process status, clear IEEE flags or promise a particular processor representation.

pending.stop-code-output: PENDING complete true-QUIET runs with independently known default-integer/default-character codes and a qualified observation of potential code-output channels. Establish statement entry and actual termination so silence cannot pass when the statement or whole program was omitted. No code-output baseline is mandated when QUIET is false, because p3 recommends it.
pending.signaling-exception-output: PENDING true-QUIET suppression with the same genuinely signaling supported flag setup that qualifies S11.4-004's mandatory false/omitted-QUIET warning. Preserve IEEE scoping/halting and ERROR_UNIT-routing premises; a flag that was never signaling is not a successful suppression witness.
pending.combined-code-and-flags: PENDING a complete true-QUIET case with both a specified code and qualified signaling flags, checking both suppression obligations without treating disappearance of only one as completion. Keep any original user-output sentinel separate from processor code/exception reports.
pending.defined-quiet-expression: PENDING a defined ordinary logical variable/expression whose independently known value is true, with a false-valued counterpart where the exact p3 premises hold. No short-circuit assumption, affected-output self-oracle or undeclared default-kind restriction.
pending.statement-kind-and-completion-guards: PENDING STOP and ERROR STOP lifecycle variants with independently observed pretermination work, externally captured process/image completion and guards against continued execution. Missing after-STOP text alone is insufficient; timeouts, crashes, launcher failures and skipped invocations cannot count as quiet termination.

requirements.oracle: A real executed true-QUIET statement and established code/flag premises, observed through qualified output and lifecycle interfaces. Literal independent setup expectations and complete traces must distinguish suppression from absent work or failed execution.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No universal empty-stderr or empty-all-output assertion, forced zero/nonzero status, C interface, flush guarantee or physical descriptor claim. Stop-code availability and status/output recommendations retain their separate meanings. Missing mode/profile/routing/lifecycle support leaves evidence unqualified; all new facets are pending.

accounting.rationale: The alternatives are expressions; no literal-only or constant-expression qualification is written.

The two execution effects are separated at the preserved child anchors. S11.4-001 remains byte-equivalent as a requirement; ERROR STOP receives a distinct pending entry, with5.3.7 retaining canonical program/image termination semantics.

The first sentence requires processor-dependent code availability; subsequent status recommendations are classified separately below. The original S11.4-001 relationship is retained only for its unchanged explicit profile qualification.

The original verb is recommended, conditional on the processor supporting process exit status. Preserve this anchor and the entire existing S11.4-001 requirement/profile calibration; correcting the source disposition does not generalize status200 or rewrite its historical fixture review. PENDING any other explicitly qualified processor/profile mapping.

The process-status concept is a condition of the recommendation, not a universally supplied Fortran interface. PENDING specific documentary/interface qualification; lack of documentation is not itself a new conformance diagnostic.

The integer value is the recommended status for either statement kind, subject to the actual processor interface. PENDING independently qualified mappings outside the frozen normal-STOP status200 case; no universal numeric range or truncation rule.

Preserve the old anchor while fully separating the STOP-character, STOP-absent, END-program, ERROR-STOP-character and ERROR-STOP-absent branches below. These are qualified recommendations, not new mandatory execution effects or completed facets.

PENDING a documented process-status/profile relation for STOP with a character code: zero is recommended if the processor supports process exit status. The character's availability is a separate S11.4-003 obligation.
PENDING a qualified processor/profile relation for STOP without a code: zero is recommended, not mandated. No absent stop-code value is invented.
PENDING the separately qualified zero-status recommendation on execution of end-program-stmt. Normal termination retains5.3.7/14.1 ownership; no duplicate END or STOP execution is added.
PENDING a processor-qualified nonzero-status recommendation for ERROR STOP with a character code. The value is processor dependent and is not proof by itself of error/image termination.
PENDING the corresponding processor-dependent nonzero-status recommendation for ERROR STOP without a code. A particular status, signal or trap is not universally required.

Both the normal zero-status and error nonzero-status recommendations depend on support for the process-status concept. PENDING real interface/profile qualification, never a generic shell-status oracle.

The error branch recommends a nonzero value chosen by the processor; it does not prescribe 1,200, a signal encoding or a universal map from a character code. PENDING documentary/profile evidence, with no count-filling S execution requirement.

Under the omitted-or-false QUIET condition, the first bullet requires an identifying ERROR_UNIT warning for signaling exceptions. The code-output second bullet is only recommended and has separate records below.

The second bullet recommends formatted code output when QUIET is omitted/false and a code is specified. PENDING exact processor documentary/profile/output qualification; do not turn this into the first bullet's mandatory warning or infer a universal message.
The code-output recommendation is conditional on a specified stop code. PENDING source-valid absent/code-present contrasts without requiring a synthetic message for an absent code.

Formatted output is the recommended method here, not a universal code-availability channel or prescribed English/encoding/format. PENDING a reviewed actual processor method; retain S11.4-003's distinct availability obligation.

The recommended code output uses the same ERROR_UNIT named in the warning bullet. PENDING actual routing qualification, including the possibility that ERROR_UNIT equals OUTPUT_UNIT; no hard-coded OS descriptor.
Explicit true QUIET requires suppression of both exception and code output. This is not weakened to recommendation or satisfied by an unexecuted program.

The expected processor-dependent multi-image summary is in an informative note, not an extra mandatory output, global warning count or execution requirement. It does not override the normative QUIET conditions.
The example context is normal termination on more than one image, not a definition of ERROR STOP propagation or failed-image behavior.
Any summary method remains processor dependent. No total ordering, one-message-per-image or fixed summary format is promised.
The note mentions stop codes and signaling exceptions together but adds no predicate beyond the normative availability/reporting/suppression rules.

The complete separate NOTE2 is on physical PDF229 before11.5. It warns conditionally about representable host exit-status ranges/portions; the low-eight-bit example is not a universal language or POSIX-profile rule.
The warning applies if an integer code is used as process exit status; it does not require that mapping or a process-status concept.
A processor might interpret only a limited range. No specific boundary or requirement that all Fortran integers fit the host status is stated.
A processor might interpret only part of the integer value. Any actual transformation needs its own processor/profile evidence.
Least-significant eight bits is an example, not a mandated modulo256, sign convention, status width or crash encoding.

ExistingS11.4-001requirement/inputs/FP/review and its explicitPOSIXstatus200profile remain exact. p2.integer-status accounting is now correctly recommendation, not permission, without rewriting the unchanged case oracle.
